record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.original_question: Do there exist an integer t and an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every n, the maximum size g_{K_{t,t}}(n) of a family of graphs on [n] in which any two graphs intersect in a copy of the complete bipartite graph K_{t,t} satisfies g_{K_{t,t}}(n) ≤ (1 - c) 2^{(n choose 2) - 1}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.6. There exists t ∈ N and an absolute constant c > 0 such that gKt,t(n) ≤ (1 − c)2^((n choose 2)−1) for all n ∈ N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a graph H, let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of (labelled) graphs on the vertex set $[n] = \{1,2,\dots,n\}$. Say that $\mathcal{F}$ is H-intersecting if for any two graphs $G_1, G_2 \in \mathcal{F}$, the intersection $G_1 \cap G_2$ (the graph on $[n]$ whose edge set is $E(G_1) \cap E(G_2)$) contains a copy of $H$ as a subgraph. Define
$$g_H(n) = \max\{|\mathcal{F}| : \mathcal{F} \text{ is an } H\text{-intersecting family of graphs on } [n]\}.$$
For positive integers $t$, let $K_{t,t}$ denote the complete bipartite graph with parts of size $t$.

Question: Do there exist a positive integer $t$ and an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that
$$g_{K_{t,t}}(n) \le (1 - c)\, 2^{\binom{n}{2} - 1}$$
for all positive integers $n$?
